LESSON: CONSERVING FOOD NUTRIENTS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Conservation of Resources
Topic 1.3: Conserving Food Nutrients

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Conserving Food Nutrients. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we conserve vitamins and minerals in vegetables?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify ways of conserving vitamins and minerals in vegetables

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify ways of conserving vitamins and minerals in vegetables
   In simple words: practise until you can identify ways of conserving vitamins and minerals in vegetables. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Conserving Food Nutrients using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Conserving Food Nutrients in the examples.
2. Explain Conserving Food Nutrients to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Conserving Food Nutrients.
4. Show that you can: identify ways of conserving vitamins and minerals in vegetables

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Conserving Food Nutrients using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Conserving Food Nutrients important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Search for information and discuss on ways of conserving vitamins and minerals in vegetables such as washing, peeling, cutting, cooking time, and covering.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify ways of conserving vitamins and minerals in vegetables

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
